name: Streak
tagline: Build a simple pipeline beside a local mailbox index without embedding inside Gmail

tiers.name: Free email power tools
tiers.limits: Mail merge 50 emails/day plus email/link tracking, snippets, Streak Share and Thread Splitter; no paid-plan CRM record entitlement stated
tiers.notes: The current pricing page describes these tools as free forever rather than presenting a full free CRM tier.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited CRM records and shared contacts; 20 AI credits/user/month; mail merge up to 1,500/day on Google Workspace (400/day personal Gmail)

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: Unlimited records; 150 AI credits/user/month; advanced reports, integrations and automations

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Minimum 10 users; 500 AI credits/user/month; custom roles, data validation and dedicated support
tiers.notes: Pricing grid displays $159/month as the month-to-month comparator, but the FAQ says Enterprise is sold only annually to teams of 10+.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free email tools: 50 mail-merge emails/day plus tracking, snippets, Streak Share and Thread Splitter; current page does not state a free CRM-record allowance
pricing.billingTerms: Pro and Pro+ monthly + annual (-20%); Enterprise annual only with 10-seat minimum
pricing.hiddenCosts: All members of a team must use the same paid plan and there is no cheaper view-only seat. AI credits do not roll over; recurring add-ons cost $100/month for 1,000, $200 for 2,500, $500 for 10,000 or $1,000 for 25,000 credits. Advanced implementation can carry a separate fee.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Streak, build a simple pipeline beside a local mailbox index without embedding inside Gmail. The hard boundary is deep gmail integration, shared mailboxes, email tracking, automations, and team adoption, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies beside a local mailbox index, move opportunities through a simple pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action without embedding inside Gmail.
whatYouLose: deep Gmail integration, shared mailboxes, email tracking, automations, and team adoption
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Streak because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or upload the PHP package and run the web installer
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in a self-hosted MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded files in server/Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: EspoCRM does not live inside Gmail, so turning messages into pipeline records and updating them requires switching to a separate application.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, database, domain/TLS setup, and ongoing upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: One-click Frappe Cloud signup or the official Python easy-install deployment script on your server
facts.dataFormat: CRM DocType records and attachments in the Frappe site database/files, on Frappe Cloud or the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe CRM can connect mailboxes, but the pipeline remains a separate web app rather than a native part of Gmail.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use means self-hosting; the official production script still needs a Linux server, DNS, and command-line access

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot’s Gmail extension still depends on a separate CRM and does not turn the inbox itself into Streak’s native pipeline workspace.

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty can synchronize a mailbox, but it does not embed pipeline rows and CRM editing directly inside Gmail as Streak does.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: A three-user pipeline with Gmail integration; not embedded, not elegant, still functional.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM service data stored on Zoho's cloud servers; Zoho states users can access, export, and delete service data
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho’s Gmail connection is an integration beside the CRM, not the native inbox-embedded pipeline that distinguishes Streak.

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted pipeline with Google Calendar sync and email activities; Gmail remains next door.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo can log email activities, but Gmail remains a separate surface rather than the CRM’s primary interface.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A standalone three-user pipeline with built-in email; no Gmail sidebar required.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM records and uploaded files stored in Freshworks' cloud; account data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Freshsales provides a standalone inbox and CRM rather than Streak’s pipeline directly inside Gmail.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Streak in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies beside a local mailbox index, move opportunities through a simple pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action without embedding inside Gmail.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
